Nor a mute that is followed by a spirant --- provided the following spirant is likewise in the same case.
Of grave syllables following a circumflex in sa[?]hit[?] there is pracaya[,] having the tone of acute.
But not when an acute or circumflex follows.
After a non-nasal mute[,] when it is followed by a nasal[,] are inserted[,] in theri order[,] nose-sounds.
Some call these yamas.
After h[,] when followed by n[,] [?][,] or m[,] is inserted n[?]sikya.
In the combination of r and a spirant[,] there is a svarabhakti of r.
But not in case of krama[,] when a first mute follows the spirant.
Tone is the material of all articulate sounds.
In the difference of form of the former consists the difference of the latter.
Here we will instance the offices of terms.
varu[?]a and k[?]ra are indicatory.
ca and api are implicative.
tu[,] atha[,] and eva are exceptional[,] introductory[,] and restrictive[,] respectively.
v[?] is alternative.
na is prohibitive.
Tension[,] hardness[,] smallness of aperture[,] are producers of high tone.
Relaxation[,] softness[,] wideness of aperture[,] are producers of low tone.
Soft[,] middle[,] and loud are the three qualities.
In them are twenty-one tones.

items.text_devanagari: ऋग्विरामः पदविरामो विवृत्तिविरामः समानपदविवृत्तिविरामस्त्रिमात्रो द्विमात्र एकमात्रो ऽर्धमात्र इत्यानुऊर्व्येण।
items.text_iast: ṛgvirāmaḥ padavirāmo vivṛttivirāmaḥ samānapadavivṛttivirāmastrimātro dvimātra ekamātro 'rdhamātra ityānuūrvyeṇa|
items.text_slp1: fgvirAmaH padavirAmo vivfttivirAmaH samAnapadavivfttivirAmastrimAtro dvimAtra ekamAtro 'rDamAtra ityAnuUrvyeRa.
items.translation_whitney: The verse-pause[,] pada-pause[,] pause for hiatus[,] and pause for hiatus in the interior of a word[,] are respectively of three moras[,] two moras[,] one mora[,] anda a half-mora.

items.text_devanagari: यद्यञ्जनान्तं यदु चापि दीर्घं संयोगपूर्वं च तथानुनासिकम्। एतानि सर्वाणि गुरूणि विद्याच् छेषाण्यतो ऽन्यानि ततो लघूनि।
items.text_iast: yadyañjanāntaṃ yadu cāpi dīrghaṃ saṃyogapūrvaṃ ca tathānunāsikam| etāni sarvāṇi gurūṇi vidyāc cheṣāṇyato 'nyāni tato laghūni|
items.text_slp1: yadyaYjanAntaM yadu cApi dIrGaM saMyogapUrvaM ca taTAnunAsikam. etAni sarvARi gurURi vidyAc CezARyato 'nyAni tato laGUni.
items.translation_whitney: A syllable that ends with a consonat[,] one that has a long vowel[,] one that preceedes a conjuction of consonants[,] one that is nasal --- all these are to be accounted heavy; the rest[,] other than these[,] are light.

items.text_devanagari: अव्यञ्जनान्तं यद्ध्रस्वमसंयोगपरं च यत्। अननुस्वारसंयुक्तमेतल्लघु निषोधतै तल्लघु निबोधत।
items.text_iast: avyañjanāntaṃ yaddhrasvamasaṃyogaparaṃ ca yat| ananusvārasaṃyuktametallaghu niṣodhatai tallaghu nibodhata|
items.text_slp1: avyaYjanAntaM yadDrasvamasaMyogaparaM ca yat . ananusvArasaMyuktametallaGu nizoDatE tallaGu niboData.
items.translation_whitney: A syllable that does not end with a consonat[,] that has a short vowel[,] and that is not followed by a conjunction of consonants[,] and one that is not combined with anusv[?]ra --- know that to be light.
Now for the origin of the differences of articulate sounds.

items.text_slp1: anupradAnAtsaMsargAtsTAnAtkaraRavinyayAt . jAyate varRavESezyaM parimARAcca paYcamAd iti.
items.translation_whitney: The differentiation of articulate sounds arises from emission[,] closure[,] position[,] disposition of producing organ[,] and[,] fifthly[,] from quantity.
Sound combined with articulation is the orgin of voice.
Of voice[,] there are seven qualities.
Namely[,] inaudible[,] murmur[,] whisper[,] mumbling[,] soft[,] middle[,] and loud.
"Inaudible" is without sound[,] without application of mind[,] but with articulating action.
"Murmur" is inaudibleness of syllables and consonants.
"Whisper" is their audibleness.
"Mumbling" is the same[,] with sound.

items.text_devanagari: उरसि मन्द्रं कण्ठे मध्यमं शिरसि तारम्।
items.text_iast: urasi mandraṃ kaṇṭhe madhyamaṃ śirasi tāram|
items.text_slp1: urasi mandraM kaRWe maDyamaM Sirasi tAram.
items.translation_whitney: "Soft" is in the chest[,] "middle" in the throat[,] "loud" in the head.
In the three qualities beginning with "soft[,]" there are seven tones each.
Namely[,] k[?][?][?]a[,] first[,] second[,] third[,] fourth[,] mandra[,] and atisv[?]rya.
Of these[,] the perception is born of brightness.
"Second[,]" "first[,]" and k[?][?][?]a are the three tones of the [?]hv[?]rakas.
The four beginning with mandra and ending with "second" are those of the taittir[?]yas.
According to the taittir[?]yas[,] the mandra proceeds from the "second[,]" and the "third" and "fourth" come next after: this they style the tone-quaternion.
In it[,] progression is by intervals of two tones.
That progression we will set forth.
That is what is called the quaternion of tones.

items.text_devanagari: क्रमिवक्रमसंपन्नामद्रुतामविलम्बिताम्। नीचोच्चस्वारसंपन्नां वदेद्धृतवतीं समां वदेद्धृतवतीं समामिति।
items.text_iast: kramivakramasaṃpannāmadrutāmavilambitām| nīcoccasvārasaṃpannāṃ vadeddhṛtavatīṃ samāṃ vadeddhṛtavatīṃ samāmiti|
items.text_slp1: kramivakramasaMpannAmadrutAmavilambitAm . nIcoccasvArasaMpannAM vadedDftavatIM samAM vadedDftavatIM samAmiti.
items.translation_whitney: It must be uttered with krama and vikrama[,] not hurried[,] not delayed[,] with grave[,] acute[,] and circumflex accent[,] with pracaya[,] and even.
Now for the four texts.
Word-text[,] syllable-text[,] letter-text[,] and member-text[,] namely.
Conjuction of independent words by euphonic combination is called word-text.
And in like manner with the syllable-text and the rest[,] in accordance with their several names.

items.text_devanagari: गुरुत्वं लघुता साम्यं ह्रस्वदीर्घप्लुतानि च। लोपागमविकाराश्च प्रकृतिर्विक्रमः क्रमः। स्वरितोदात्तनीचत्वं श्वासो नादो ऽङ्गमेव च। एतत्सर्वं तु विज्ञेयं छन्दोभाषामधीयता।
items.text_iast: gurutvaṃ laghutā sāmyaṃ hrasvadīrghaplutāni ca| lopāgamavikārāśca prakṛtirvikramaḥ kramaḥ| svaritodāttanīcatvaṃ śvāso nādo 'ṅgameva ca| etatsarvaṃ tu vijñeyaṃ chandobhāṣāmadhīyatā|
items.text_slp1: gurutvaM laGutA sAmyaM hrasvadIrGaplutAni ca . lopAgamavikArASca prakftirvikramaH kramaH. svaritodAttanIcatvaM SvAso nAdo 'Ngameva ca . etatsarvaM tu vijYeyaM CandoBAzAmaDIyatA.
items.translation_whitney: Heaviness[,] lightness[,] evenness; short[,] long[,] and protracted quantity; elision[,] increment[,] and euphonic alteration; natural state[,] vikrama[,] krama; circumflex[,] acute[,] and grave quality; breath[,] tone[,] and adjunction --- all this must be understod by him who reads the Veda language.
He who understands the distinctions of the pada-krama[,] who is versed in the var[?]a-krama[,] and knows the divisions of accent and quantity[,] may go and sit with the teachers.
